statement: In the low-friction high-mass region, the current grip force is insufficient to prevent slip during lift, causing MISSED_GRASP and SLIPPED_ON_LIFT.
mechanism: Required grip force scales with mass / friction; at 15 N the friction force is too low to hold heavy cubes with low friction.
prediction: Increasing grip_force will reduce MISSED_GRASP and SLIPPED_ON_LIFT failure rates in this region.

statement: For very small cubes combined with high gripper delay, the grasp hold time is too short for the fingers to securely close, leading to MISSED_GRASP.
mechanism: High gripper delay postpones the close command; small cubes have less contact area and need more hold steps to stabilize before lift.
prediction: Increasing grasp_hold_steps will reduce MISSED_GRASP failures in this region.

statement: In the low-friction high-sensor-noise region, perception errors cause misaligned grasps that slip; retries with fresh perception could recover.
mechanism: Low friction amplifies the effect of grasp misalignment from sensor noise; retries allow re-perception and re-grasp.
prediction: Setting retry_count > 0 will reduce MISSED_GRASP failures in this region.

statement: For heavy small cubes, the lift speed generates inertial forces that exceed the friction limit, causing SLIPPED_ON_LIFT.
mechanism: High mass and small size imply high density; rapid acceleration during lift creates inertial load that overcomes friction.
prediction: Decreasing lift_speed will reduce SLIPPED_ON_LIFT failures in this region.
